newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to hesitate crossing above 4,700.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to hesitate crossing above 4,700.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will show hesitancy in marching higher on Tuesday although it may be able to cross above the 4,700 level later in the day but it will show reluctance to stay above it, technical analysts said.

Banks and insurance shares, which have boosted the index recently owing in part to a firmer gilts market, will again make for a firm market and it may also be pulled higher by strength in pharmaceuticals and utilities, they added.
Further help also may come from a positive trend in the gilts market.
By 0739 GMT, the FTSE was up 1.3 at 4,688.0.

Breadth and momentum readings for the FTSE have been adjusting quickly and no longer show the market as being oversold but the pace of further share price rises will begin to slow down, analysts said.
And without some consolidation or a little retracing of the 130 point advance by the FTSE over the past four days, the market could soon run out of its current enthusiasm.

Market breadth yesterday was seven-to-three in favour of advancing stocks and analysts expect this to decline slightly today. And with the FTSE's 10 day momentum now giving a neutral reading, the market may begin to flatten out, they added.
